what_it_does: Neural image compression uses AI models to squeeze photos into fewer bytes than traditional formats like JPEG, but it normally requires a powerful encoder and decoder that are both too heavy to run on a tiny Internet-of-Things (IoT) sensor. Easz solves this by splitting the work asymmetrically: the edge device does almost nothing — it just erases (patches out) selected regions of the image using a lightweight algorithm — and sends the sparse result to a server, which runs a small transformer-based neural network (a type of AI that processes data in parallel chunks) to reconstruct the missing pixels. Because the heavy computation lives on the server, the IoT device needs very little processing power or memory. The system can also adapt to different compression levels without switching between multiple trained models, which saves storage. The abstract reports evaluation on a real physical testbed, but detailed accuracy and latency figures are not available here.
